documents.title: Why the four-day week stalled at Norvik Insurance
documents.text:
Two years ago, Norvik Insurance announced a pilot in which its 900 office staff would work four days a week for the same pay. Early reports were glowing: absenteeism fell by a third and a staff survey found that eight in ten employees felt less stressed. Yet last month, the company quietly confirmed that the experiment would not be extended beyond the claims department.

According to chief executive Olga Brandt, the difficulty lay not with productivity, which was largely maintained, but with coordination. Departments that remained on five days found it hard to reach colleagues on Fridays, and customers complained that advisers were unavailable when they called. [A] "We had solved one problem and created another," she says. Attempts to stagger days off complicated the schedule further, with several managers reporting that they spent more time arranging cover than managing their teams.

Employees are divided on the outcome. Some, such as claims handler Dario Estevez, argue that the company gave up too soon: "We showed that it works if everyone commits to it." Others admit that the extra day was often spent catching up on e-mails from the previous week. [B] Ms. Brandt says the company is now exploring a compromise in which employees may compress their hours into four longer days, though this would not reduce the total hours worked. Labor analysts suggest that firms attempting similar changes should consider clients' habits at least as carefully as their own staff's wishes. [C]

questions.prompt: What is the article mainly about?
choices: A fall in the number of claims made by customers
The limited continuation of a shorter working week
A company's plan to hire more telephone advisers
A dispute over pay between managers and staff
questions.explanation: The pilot of a four-day week has been confined to one department because of coordination problems.

questions.prompt: What does Ms. Brandt identify as the main difficulty?
choices: A decline in the output of the employees
The higher salaries demanded by many staff
The cost of equipment needed for remote work
Schedules that did not match between departments
questions.explanation: Productivity held up; the problem was coordination between departments and with customers.

questions.prompt: What can be inferred about Mr. Estevez?
choices: He would have preferred the trial to go on
He has requested a transfer to another department
He now works four longer days each week
He is responsible for scheduling cover
questions.explanation: He says the company gave up too soon and that the scheme works if everyone commits.

questions.prompt: In which position marked [A], [B], [C] or [D] does the following sentence best belong? "Customers, in other words, did not adapt to the new rhythm as quickly as the staff did."
questions.explanation: The sentence generalizes the point about clients' habits made in the sentence before [C]; elsewhere it would break the argument about managers or staff opinions.

documents.title: Introduction of new laboratory safety rules
documents.text:
To: All research staff, Halden Institute
From: Dr. Margit Solheim, Safety Officer
Subject: Changes to laboratory access, effective 3 November

Dear colleagues,

Following two minor incidents in the past quarter, the Safety Committee has approved new rules for out-of-hours access to the laboratories. In neither incident was anyone hurt, but in both cases the person present was working alone and could not immediately call for assistance.

From 3 November, nobody may work in a wet laboratory between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m. unless a second person is present in the same building. Researchers who must run experiments overnight, for example long incubations, should register in advance using the online form, naming their companion. The security desk will not release keys for these rooms without a confirmed registration. Computational work and writing are not covered by the rule and may continue in the offices.

I recognize that this may be inconvenient, particularly for doctoral students whose experiments follow biological rhythms. For that reason, the Committee will review the policy at the end of January and invites your feedback through the staff forum. Mandatory refresher training on emergency procedures will be held on 28 October, and attendance will be recorded.

choices: Two employees were seriously injured at night
Keys to the laboratories had been mislaid
Staff working alone were unable to get quick help
The institute's insurance had been changed
questions.explanation: In both incidents nobody was hurt, but the person present was alone and could not immediately call for help.

questions.prompt: Who is NOT affected by the new rule?
choices: Researchers carrying out evening experiments

People writing reports in the offices
Anyone who needs keys for a wet laboratory
questions.explanation: Computational work and writing are not covered by the rule and may continue in the offices.

It will be dropped at the end of the year

questions.explanation: The Committee will review the policy at the end of January and invites feedback.

documents.title: Closure of the Elmstead swimming pool
documents.text:
The Elmstead Leisure Centre announces that its main swimming pool will close for essential maintenance from Monday 5 January until Friday 27 February. During this period, the smaller training pool will remain open, though it will operate to a reduced timetable: weekdays from 6:30 to 9:00 a.m. and from 5:00 to 8:00 p.m., and on weekends from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Lane swimming will be limited to members.

The work includes replacing the filtration system, resurfacing the pool floor and installing a lift for wheelchair users. Because the lift requires a section of the changing room to be rebuilt, the accessible changing cubicles will also be unavailable for the first three weeks; a temporary alternative will be provided in the sports hall. Swimming lessons for children will continue in the training pool, but class sizes will be reduced, and some groups will be moved to Saturday mornings. Parents will be contacted individually by 12 December.

Members will receive a credit of 15 percent of their monthly fee for each month of closure. Casual visitors may use the facility only on weekends during this time. We apologize for any inconvenience and look forward to welcoming you to a modernized facility.

choices: To announce the opening of a new pool for all
To increase the fee for casual visitors only
To tell users about a temporary change to services
To invite parents to a swimming contest
questions.explanation: The notice describes a closure and the alternative arrangements.

choices: A larger changing room for children's groups

A lift for people with limited mobility

questions.explanation: The work includes installing a lift for wheelchair users.

questions.explanation: The pool is open on weekdays from 5:00 to 8:00 p.m., but casual visitors may use the facility only on weekends.

documents.title: Customer Success Manager, Lumen Software
documents.text:
Lumen Software, a provider of scheduling tools for clinics, is seeking a Customer Success Manager to join our Dublin office. You will be responsible for a portfolio of around sixty clinics, ensuring that they adopt the product fully and renew their contracts. The role involves running training sessions, analyzing usage data and passing on customer feedback to our developers.

You should have at least three years of experience in a customer-facing role at a software company, strong presentation skills, and a good understanding of how healthcare organizations operate. Fluency in English is required; a second European language is valued. The post is hybrid, with three days in the office, and involves occasional travel of up to five days per quarter.

Salary range: 52,000 to 60,000 euros, plus a bonus of up to ten percent linked to customer retention. To apply, send a cover letter describing a situation in which you saved a client relationship, together with your résumé, to jobs@lumensoftware.example by 21 February. Interviews will take place in the first week of March.

documents.title: Application: Customer Success Manager
documents.text:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I would like to apply for the position of Customer Success Manager. For the past five years I have worked at Medisched, a competitor, where I manage forty-five hospital accounts. Last spring, one of my largest clients threatened to cancel after a system outage; by organizing weekly calls and training their staff on a backup procedure, I helped retain the contract, worth 180,000 euros a year.

I was a nurse for six years before moving into software, which gives me a practical understanding of how clinics schedule appointments. I speak English and Spanish fluently. My only concern is the travel requirement: I have a young child and would prefer to limit trips to three days per quarter. I would be grateful if you could tell me whether that would be acceptable.

Yours sincerely,
Orla Whelan

documents.title: Re: Application: Customer Success Manager
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Whelan,

Thank you for applying. Your experience is exactly what we are looking for, and the committee would like to meet you on Tuesday 4 March at 11:00. Regarding travel, the five days mentioned in the advertisement are a maximum rather than a requirement, so three days should be feasible. However, you would be responsible for sixty accounts, rather than forty-five, and we expect new clients to be added during the year.

For the interview, please prepare a ten-minute presentation on how you would improve the adoption of a new feature among clinics that have been reluctant to change. Could you confirm by Friday?

Best wishes,
Declan Foley, Head of Customer Success

documents.title: Greenfield Farm Box: How it works
documents.text:
Our weekly boxes contain vegetables and fruit grown within thirty miles of your door. Choose a small box (serves two, 22 dollars) or a family box (serves four, 34 dollars). Deliveries are made on Thursday evenings between 5 and 8 p.m. To skip a week, change your order in your account before midnight on the preceding Sunday. Orders can be paused for up to six weeks per year without penalty.

Extras: Add eggs (6 dollars), sourdough bread (5 dollars) or a bottle of cold-pressed juice (4 dollars) to any box. New customers receive a free jar of honey with their first delivery. Our boxes are packed in reusable crates, which are collected on your next delivery; please leave them clean and empty by your door.

documents.title: Question about my box
documents.text:
Hello,

I started my subscription three weeks ago with a family box. I'll be away from 10 to 24 November and would like to pause deliveries, but I can't see how to do that on the Web site. Also, last Thursday the delivery arrived at 9:30 p.m., after the children had gone to bed, and one of the crates was left on the doorstep in the rain. Is there any way to make sure it arrives earlier? And can I switch to the small box permanently, since we throw away too much?

Thanks,
Joanne Whitaker

documents.title: Re: Question about my box
documents.text:
Dear Ms. Whitaker,

I apologize for the late delivery; our driver was delayed by roadworks. As a gesture, I have added a free loaf of sourdough to your next box. To pause, please e-mail me the dates, which I will enter manually since the feature is being fixed. The deliveries for 13 and 20 November would be skipped, and your order resumes on 27 November. Changing to the small box is simple: I have done so from your next delivery, so you will be charged 22 dollars instead of 34.

Unfortunately we cannot guarantee a time slot earlier than 5 p.m., but I have asked the driver to call before arriving.

Regards,
Hamza Qureshi, Customer Care

documents.title: Council to review night-time economy rules
documents.text:
A committee of the Marburn City Council will meet on Thursday to consider changes to the licensing rules that govern bars and clubs in the Old Quarter. The review follows a petition signed by 1,200 residents who complain of noise and litter after midnight. Under the existing rules, venues may remain open until 3 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays; the petition calls for a 1 a.m. closing time.

Business owners have responded with alarm. The Old Quarter Business Association says that the area's nightlife contributes an estimated 14 million dollars to the local economy each year and that an earlier closing time would force several venues to shut down. Association chair Ravi Nair argues that the problem lies with enforcement rather than opening hours. "A handful of premises cause most of the trouble," he says. "Punish them, not everyone."

A compromise is under discussion. Councillor Irene Falk has proposed that venues be allowed to open until 2 a.m. provided that they join a scheme under which they contribute to extra street cleaning and security patrols. The scheme, which has operated successfully in the neighboring town of Lisle, would be reviewed after a year. Residents' spokesperson Anneke Visser says that she is open to the idea but wants strict penalties for venues that break the terms. The committee is expected to vote in January.

questions.prompt: What is the main subject of the article?
choices: The opening of a new club in the Old Quarter
A cleaning program carried out by the council
The cost of police patrols in neighboring towns
A debate about the closing times of nightlife venues
questions.explanation: The article reports on a review of licensing rules, residents' petition, business objections and a compromise.

questions.prompt: What is Mr. Nair's view?
choices: Only troublesome venues should be penalized
All venues should close at 1 a.m. sharp
Residents should simply accept the noise
The council should pay for extra patrols itself
questions.explanation: He says a handful of premises cause most trouble and asks to punish them, not everyone.

questions.prompt: Which closing time would the proposal by Ms. Falk introduce?
choices: 1 a.m. for all venues
3 a.m. for venues in neighboring towns
2 a.m. for venues that join the scheme
Midnight on weekdays only
questions.explanation: Venues would be allowed to open until 2 a.m. provided that they join a scheme paying for cleaning and security.

questions.prompt: The word "alarm" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to
choices: noise
excitement
concern
warning device
questions.explanation: Business owners are worried that an earlier closing time would harm them.

Payment may be made by bank transfer or by check made out to Parkside Landscaping Ltd; please quote the invoice number. Late payments are subject to interest at 1.5 percent per month. Payment terms: balance due within 30 days. Work carried out is guaranteed for 12 months; plants are replaced free of charge during the first three months if they fail.

documents.title: Re: Invoice 7731
documents.text:
Dear Mr. Moore,

Thank you for your note. Regarding the trees: I understand that two of the five are showing yellow leaves, which sometimes happens after planting in dry weather. Because we are within the three-month period, we will replace them at no cost, and I can send a crew next Tuesday. I would, however, ask that your staff water them every second day until then; this is not covered by the guarantee if neglected.

As for the paving, the area was measured at 85 square meters on site, and I attach the sketch. If you believe it is smaller, please send your own measurement and we will check it together.

The remaining balance remains payable on the original terms; however, if the replacement of the two trees is completed before the due date, I am happy to confirm in writing that no further charge will be made for that work. I would also recommend a short inspection visit in the autumn, which we offer free of charge to every client in the first year.

Regards,
Paula Sandoval
